correctness.rationale: For nonempty rows \(R_i\) and \(R_j\) with \(i<j\), forward confluence is equivalent to \(\max R_i<\max R_j\): the later maximum witnesses every earlier element, while failure at the earlier maximum is decisive. Backward confluence is equivalently \(\min R_i<\min R_j\). Hence total expansiveness is exactly strict increase of both endpoint sequences. The existence condition \(m\le n\), the minimum-size functional relations counted by \(\binom{n}{m}\), and the maximum \(m(n-m+1)\) with interval rows follow from the available slack in the two strict endpoint sequences. A fresh exhaustive replay for all relations with \(m,n\le3\) reproduced the endpoint criterion, zero counts for \(m>n\), and all size extrema.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns finite strict chains and source-total relations; it does not classify arbitrary transitive frames or require target-totality.
